hints: Multiply every term by $x^{1/2}$ to get $2x + 13 = 3 + 12x^{1/2} \implies 2x - 12x^{1/2} + 10 = 0$.
Divide by $2$ and factorise the quadratic in $x^{1/2}$: $(x^{1/2} - 1)(x^{1/2} - 5) = 0$.
Find $x = 1$ and $x = 25$, then calculate the corresponding $y$-coordinates.
walkthrough:
Equate the two curve equations to find their points of intersection:
$$2x^{1/2} + 13x^{-1/2} = 3x^{-1/2} + 12$$

Divide by $2$ and factorise as a quadratic in $x^{1/2}$:
$$x - 6x^{1/2} + 5 = 0 \implies (x^{1/2} - 1)(x^{1/2} - 5) = 0$$
$$x^{1/2} = 1 \implies x = 1$$
$$x^{1/2} = 5 \implies x = 25$$

Calculate the corresponding $y$-coordinates using $y = 3x^{-1/2} + 12$:
$$\text{For } x = 1: \quad y = 3(1) + 12 = 15 \implies A(1, 15)$$
$$\text{For } x = 25: \quad y = 3\left(\frac{1}{5}\right) + 12 = 0.6 + 12 = 12.6 \implies B(25, 12.6)$$
$$\text{(or } B(25, 13) \text{ as written in mark scheme)}$$

hints: Set up the integral for the area between the curves: $\int_1^{25} \left( (3x^{-1/2} + 12) - (2x^{1/2} + 13x^{-1/2}) \right) dx = \int_1^{25} (-2x^{1/2} + 12 - 10x^{-1/2})\, dx$.
Evaluate at limits $x = 25$ and $x = 1$, and subtract.
walkthrough:
Set up the definite integral for the area bounded between the two curves from $x = 1$ to $x = 25$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_1^{25} \left( (3x^{-1/2} + 12) - (2x^{1/2} + 13x^{-1/2}) \right) dx = \int_1^{25} \left( -2x^{1/2} + 12 - 10x^{-1/2} \right) dx$$

Integrate term by term using the power rule:
$$\int -2x^{1/2}\, dx = -2 \cdot \frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2} = -\frac{4}{3}x^{3/2}$$
$$\int 12\, dx = 12x$$
$$\int -10x^{-1/2}\, dx = -10 \cdot \frac{x^{1/2}}{1/2} = -20x^{1/2}$$
$$\text{Antiderivative} = \left[ -\frac{4}{3}x^{3/2} + 12x - 20x^{1/2} \right]_1^{25}$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = 1$ and subtract:
$$-\frac{4}{3}(1) + 12(1) - 20(1) = -\frac{4}{3} - 8 = -\frac{28}{3}$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{100}{3} - \left(-\frac{28}{3}\right) = \frac{128}{3} = 42\frac{2}{3} \approx 42.7$$
